turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry we're late, the tram was a shocker. This is Oscar, he's thirteen.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): No worries, come on through. What can I do for him today?
[SEG0003] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A kid in his class has measles, and now he's got a rash and he's been really hot.
[SEG0004] person_3 (PATIENT): I'm not sick. It's nothing.
[SEG0005] person_2 (DOCTOR): Oscar, I'd like to hear it from you too. How have you been feeling, mate?
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): Can we get Maccas after this.
[SEG0007] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll see about that later. Mum, when did this fever actually start?
[SEG0008] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Saturday arvo. So, um, four days. I checked him that night and the chemist one said thirty nine, well actually it beeped at thirty nine.
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Nah. It was like one day.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay, so between the two of you it's somewhere from one day to four days, and we won't pin it harder than that. When did the rash show up?
[SEG0011] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yesterday. Started behind his ears and then, yeah, all over the chest by bedtime.
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): Just a couple of spots. They don't bug me.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any cough, or a runny nose, or sore eyes with it?
[SEG0014] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No cough and no runny nose. His eyes have been red though, and the light's been annoying him.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting or diarrhoea? Sore throat?
[SEG0016] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting, no diarrhoea. His throat's been a bit scratchy.
[SEG0017] person_2 (DOCTOR): Oscar, what have you had for the fever, any medicine?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): I take amladipine for the pressure, five milligrams in the morning, the cholesterol one at night, sugar tablets, and only the ayurvedic powder in the morning.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Those sound like your regular ones. I was asking about something for this fever, Panadol or Nurofen. Mum, has he had any?
[SEG0020] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Panadol, yeah. Two tablets, um, two fifty? No, five hundred milligrams each, every six hours, since Saturday. He does take them.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ta. Any trouble with his breathing, or pain in the tummy?
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): We had pizza last night.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll ask that one again. Any breathing trouble or tummy pain?
[SEG0024] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, breathing's been fine and his tummy's fine. He did have pizza, that's true, but no pain.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): How are the immunisations, the measles one especially?
[SEG0026] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Err, I reckon he's had the jabs. The blue book's in the kitchen drawer. He might've missed the one around four, uh I'm not sure.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): We'll leave that as not clear and chase the record. Oscar, just so I know the family background, has anyone in the family had ongoing illnesses?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): My father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thanks, that's useful. And what's a normal week look like for you, school, food, all that?
[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): I pack shelves at the supermarket on Saturdays, about five hours, I pretty much live on two-minute noodles, I don't exercise, and I don't touch alcohol.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. I'm going to have a look at you now, Oscar. Shirt up if that's okay.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Whatever. Hurry up.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Temp is thirty eight point four, pulse a hundred and twenty, breathing twenty two, oxygen ninety eight percent, and blood pressure one hundred and ten over seventy.

[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): There's a blotchy red rash over the face, behind the ears and across the trunk. Inside the cheeks I can see small white spots, those are Koplik spots. Chest is clear and the neck isn't stiff.
[SEG0035] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Those white spots, is that bad?

[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): They fit with measles, along with the timing. If we go with your four days of fever, today is day four, and the rash came yesterday which is about day three, and that's the classic window. I can't call it confirmed yet. It might still be another viral rash, but measles is the one I'm most worried about given the classmate.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): I said I'm fine.

[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): I hear you, mate, and I still want to be careful. We'll keep you home from school, no visitors, especially no babies and no one who's pregnant, until four days after the rash began.
[SEG0039] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So that's through the weekend, yeah?
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, rash day one was yesterday, so stay isolated until four full days from then. I'll notify the public health unit today, measles is notifiable.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll also arrange a measles PCR swab with pathology today. If that swab doesn't sort it out we might add a blood test later.
[SEG0042] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Do I keep the Panadol going?

[SEG0043] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yes, same two tablets every six hours if he's hot or sore, and push fluids. If he's drowsy, struggling to breathe, or not drinking, go straight to emergency, don't wait for me.
[SEG0044] person_3 (PATIENT): Can we go now.
[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nearly. I'll book a review here in three days, or sooner if you're worried. Can you bring the blue book next time so we can check the measles vaccine properly?
[SEG0046] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yep, I'll dig it out. Thanks for not rushing us.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): You're welcome. Any questions before you head off?
[SEG0048] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, I think I've got it. Home, no school, swab today, back in three days.
[SEG0049] person_3 (PATIENT): Finally.

spec.situation: Parents of a child with rash and fever after a classmate had measles; vaccination status vague; doctor examines, counts days, plans notification and isolation advice.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

bad.reason: Patient mentions pressure and amlodipine; ongoing implied, but hypertension diagnosis not explicitly named.

omissions.text: Exposure history: a kid/classmate in Oscar's class has measles.
Fever was measured at home as 39 C on Saturday night with a chemist thermometer.
Rash distribution/onset detail was behind the ears initially and then all over the chest by bedtime; recorded rash body site misses the 'behind the ears' wording and fuller spread description.
Immunisation status is unclear for measles/MMR; mother thinks he has had vaccinations but may have missed the one around age 4, and doctor plans to chase the record.
Family history also included that mother did not have diabetes.
Doctor advised review in three days, or sooner if worried.
